method: Every file was dropped on the shipped page through harness.js (h.file, h.text, h.rows, a DragEvent on #rfp-drop); the raw reader text is the page's own readPdf/readSheet/readDocx block copied verbatim from site/index.html and run in the page against the same File. Scripts: make_fixtures.py, make_extras.py, run.js, extras.js, extras2.js. Outputs: out/*.json.

verdicts.evidence: requirements.xlsx: '1 question found ... 1 to sort'; the one item is label '', text 'Req ID Category Requirement Priority Comply (Y/N/P) Vendor response SEC-01 Security Do you support single sign-on with SAML 2.0?', pile Not sure. FR-01 to FR-06 all vanish. Paragraphs: 'M FR-02 Content The solution shall ...', 'M FR-03 Content Describe your approach to migrating content into AEM Sites. M FR-04 Hosting The platform must ...'. SEC-02 is dropped, not merged (Opus: 2 items). Pasted as tabs, one block: 1 question, the whole matrix, pile Adobe, products cja, target, aemsites, connection aemsites+target, lines AXB02, AXB03, CJ01, C06. With a blank line between sheets: the FR block vanishes, only the SEC block survives as one unsure item.
verdicts.cause: readSheet pushes every cell as its own line and joins a cell to the next only under /^\(?[A-Za-z]?\d{0,3}(\.\d+)*[.)]?$/ && length<=8 (FR-01, REQ-04, SEC-01 fail on the hyphen and second letter); paragraphs() then glues the lines back (it breaks only on a NUM-start line or a capitalised line after a sentence end when over 80 chars) and findQuestions tests ASKS only at a sentence start, which is now the ID or header text.

verdicts.evidence: req04.xlsx (Gemini's header + row): 'no questions found'; without the header: 'no questions found' (paragraph 'REQ-04 Analytics Describe how ... conversions.'). The requirement is lost whole, not kept without its ID. Trap REQ-05 | 'Explain how you handle security' | 'System must support SSO' | Mandatory: nothing found, with or without the header. Trap with a numeric ID 4.2: label 4.2, text 'Explain how you handle security System must support SSO Mandatory', pile Not sure (category heads the text, requirement glued after it, not dropped).
verdicts.cause: Same readSheet rule; with '4.2' the numbering rule joins the ID to the next cell, which is the Category, and paragraphs() appends the Requirement and Priority cells.

verdicts.evidence: SheetJS parses the quoted newline as one cell: [['ID','Requirement','Response'],['R-1','The system must\nsupport real-time activation',''],['R-2','Describe your approach to implementing Adobe Target.','']]. The two halves rejoin in paragraphs(). But the file yields 'no questions found': one paragraph 'ID Requirement Response R-1 The system must support real-time activation R-2 Describe your approach to implementing Adobe Target.', so R-2 is lost too. With numeric IDs: '2 Describe your approach to implementing Adobe Target.' found (label 2, Target, TG01 TG02 TG03 TG05); '1 The system must support real-time activation' is one paragraph, dropped as declarative.
verdicts.cause: The CSV parse is correct; the loss is readSheet's numbering rule rejecting 'R-1'/'R-2' so the IDs become lines that paragraphs() glues onto the sentence start where ASKS fails. DeepSeek's aside that no XLSX reader ships is wrong: lib/xlsx.mini.min.js loads on first use and reads CSV.

extra.cause: accept lists .xls and readFile matches /\.(xlsx|xlsm|xls|csv)$/, but lib/xlsx.mini.min.js (SheetJS 0.18.5 mini) ships without the BIFF parser; the library's internal error reaches the status line.

extra.claim: Single-letter Priority and Comply cells meet the numbering rule, so column order decides whether a row survives

extra.cause: [A-Za-z]?\d{0,3} matches a bare letter; whether trailing cells glue onto the question depends on paragraphs()' cur.length>80 threshold.
